name: Microbiotamaxxing

card.summary: A looksmaxxing term for deliberately shaping the gut microbiome with probiotics and related protocols, aimed at skin, mood and general health.
card.note: Forum claims about autism and 'NT' effects are not supported by published studies; people with immune problems or serious illness are usually advised to consult a doctor before probiotics.

quick.overview:
Microbiotamaxxing is a forum term for optimising the bacteria in the gut, usually by taking probiotic capsules in large numbers. Proponents link a healthier microbiome to clearer skin, better mood, social ease and overall health, which they treat as part of looking and functioning better.

Probiotics are live microorganisms that, according to reviews, may alter the gut microbiome; reasonable evidence supports Lactobacillus strains in preventing antibiotic-associated diarrhea, and fecal transplant is an emerging treatment for C. difficile. Claims about autism or social behaviour made in the looksmax.org threads on this topic are not supported by trials.
quick.how: Posters describe buying live-culture capsules from health stores and taking billions of colony-forming units, sometimes asking whether doctor oversight is needed. Another post jokes about sharing cups with friends to swap bacteria.
quick.risks: Probiotic capsules are generally sold as supplements, and a forum poster asks whether high amounts need professional oversight. Reference sources describe benefits mainly for specific conditions such as antibiotic-associated diarrhea, and note that evidence in other areas is preliminary.

lead: Microbiotamaxxing is a looksmaxxing and biohacking term for improving the gut microbiome, typically with probiotic capsules. It is discussed as a route to better skin, mood and general health, which feed into appearance and social confidence.[1][2][3]

Probiotics are live microorganisms thought to benefit health by altering gut composition; prebiotics are fibres that feed beneficial bacteria.[3] Reviews say Lactobacillus probiotics may help prevent antibiotic-associated diarrhea and Saccharomyces boulardii may help prevent C. difficile infection after antibiotics, while many other areas are still preliminary.[3]
The looksmax.org threads using the term focus on large doses of live bacteria and make claims about autism that go beyond published research.[1][2]

chain: Claimed improvements in skin, mood and general condition
angle.text: Followers hope that a better gut ecosystem leads to better skin and a calmer, healthier presentation. The documented benefits of probiotics are mainly gut-related; the appearance link is what forum users claim.

infobox: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea, some IBS and IBD symptoms

paras: The term is built from 'microbiota' and the -maxxing suffix. In threads on looksmax.org, users plan to take large numbers of live bacteria, ask whether to consult a doctor and describe the aim as improving health and mood.[1][2]

Reviews describe probiotics as live microorganisms that may restore microbial balance by stimulating the immune system and reducing inflammatory cytokines.[3] Fecal microbiota transplantation is an emerging treatment for C. difficile infection, with early reports of high success rates.[3] A 2016 systematic review of preclinical and small human studies identified probiotic strains of interest for certain central nervous system disorders, and research on many other effects remains preliminary.[3]

One poster says he will take 10 billion bacteria and that this will change the balance of 'autism bacteria' and make him more neurotypical, linking to another thread he says provides citations.[2] Another asks whether to see a doctor before self-administering high amounts, saying studies show live cultures pose no risks.[1] A reply says health stores sell the cultures and that they are usually taken by people whose bacteria were depleted by medicines.[2]

No studies found for microbiotamaxxing as a practice. Studies of probiotics more broadly, summarised in reference reviews, report benefit in antibiotic-associated diarrhea and C. difficile prevention.[3]

lore.intro: Threads on looksmax.org present microbiome supplementation as a way to improve social and mental traits as well as health.[1][2]

claims.claim: Taking live bacteria reduces 'autism bacteria' and makes a person more neurotypical
claims.believers: A poster describes his plan as 'backed by science' and refers to a thread of citations.[2]
claims.experts: No published trial shows probiotics changing autism-related traits in this way; reviews describe probiotic research on the nervous system as small and preliminary.[3]

claims.claim: High amounts of live cultures carry no negative risks
claims.believers: A poster says studies show live cultures pose no negative risks, while asking if medical oversight is wise.[1]
claims.experts: Reviews cite generally good tolerability for specific uses, but evidence for self-directed high-amount use is not described.[3]
